$comment: Tunable constants for the whole game. Every number here is a dial, not a law. The web prototype reads these directly, so changing a value here changes the digital game AND the printed reference sheet.

phases.name: Events
phases.summary: In turn order, each player reveals one event card and resolves it. A card's scope decides who it hits: global cards hit everyone, whoever drew them.

phases.name: Labour Roll
phases.summary: Each player rolls their effort dice: one die per worker. Pips = hours of effort available this round.

phases.name: Actions
phases.summary: In turn order, players spend effort, coin and commodities: allocate, build, move, trade, forage, fight.

phases.name: Production Tick
phases.summary: Advance every progress track: construction, crop growth, transport in transit, maturing goods.

phases.name: Feeding
phases.summary: Each town must pay food upkeep from stock held in or near that town. Shortfalls cause unrest.

phases.name: Market
phases.summary: Market prices drift, demand cards flip, turn order passes to the left.

effort.notes: Modifiers may (a) add flat hours, (b) step a worker's die up or down the ladder, or (c) grant extra dice. Resolve in that order: extra dice, then ladder steps, then flat bonuses.

foodVarietyBonus.effect: +1 flat effort to every worker in that town next round
foodVarietyBonus.summary: Feed a town from 3+ distinct food commodities in one Feeding phase to earn the variety bonus.

starvation.riotEffect: Workers in that town roll d4 instead of their normal die until unrest clears; one worker leaves the town at 5 unrest.
starvation.clearUnrest: Feeding a town fully in a later round removes 1 unrest; a feast (2 food per worker) removes 2.

population.notes: Specialists eat like everyone else, but a town without a fed specialist cannot run recipes that require that profession.

construction.notes: Materials are paid when the site is founded. Build points accumulate on a progress track; a building only produces once its track is full.

tools.brokenToolEffect: Tool is removed from play. Effort already spent this round is not refunded.
tools.notes: Output multipliers round down, minimum 1. A size-3 tool never lets one worker exceed a site's worker cap - it just makes that worker's hours count for more.

storage.overflowRule: Commodities above capacity spoil at the end of the Feeding phase: lose half, rounded up.
storage.notes: Bulk values on commodities are slot costs. One slot holds one bulk point.

market.driftPerRound: Each town shifts one random commodity family up or down one band.

merchantStock.$comment: When a player meets a merchant - on the road via a discovery roll, or by visiting a settlement - shuffle the item deck and deal this many cards face up. That is what is for sale this visit, at base value +10%. Bigger places carry deeper stock.
merchantStock.notes: Tools may be bought the same way at any settlement with a blacksmith rank town or better: deal from the tool list instead.

market.notes: Base values live on each commodity. Town price = baseValue x band. The spread is the house cut when trading with the board rather than another player.

legs.day: Every moving figure, party or vehicle gets one day leg per round, at the speed in data/travel.json for its mode and the terrain letter codes it crosses.
legs.night: After its day leg a party may push on into the dark - but only with a lit torch or lantern, and slower. Night speeds, and what each light allows, are in data/travel.json.
legs.nightRisk: A party that travels a night leg makes a second discovery roll where it stops, with the monster band widened by 1. The dark is not neutral.

movement.notes: Figures (prospectors, merchants, soldiers, characters) use move points. Cargo uses transport modes with capacity and speed - see transport.json. The printed speed table by mode, terrain code and time of day is data/travel.json.

discovery.when: When a figure, party or vehicle ends its movement leg, roll once on the discovery table for the hex it stopped in - one roll for the leg, not one per hex crossed.
discovery.tables: data/discovery.json, one column per terrain letter code, with road and rail overrides
discovery.placement: Any result that persists - a monster, a trace, a cave, a quest site - is marked on the hex with a tile or figure so the whole table can see it.
discovery.notes: Discovery is what you find when you are NOT looking. Prospecting, foraging and hunting have their own recipes and roll tables, and a discovery roll never replaces a survey.

exploration.notes: A prospector entering a face-down tile flips it. Flipping reveals terrain immediately; deposits need a survey roll on top of that.

rest.where: Any settlement with an inn - every printed settlement has one; a player-built town needs the inn building.

cost.note: Waived in your own town, and at any inn a quest reward names.

rest.notes: A resting character does nothing else that round. Vehicle damage is repaired separately - 1 box per round in any settlement of town rank or better, paying 5 coin per box.

hirelings.where: Hired at any inn, in any settlement of village rank or better.

options.name: Thug
options.note: Refuses to fight monsters of strength 4 or more. Counts as a soldier for escort purposes.

options.name: Hired Blade
options.note: Fights anything, and rolls first like a bow.

hirelings.notes: A hireling escorts one journey - a travelling party or a cargo in transit - then goes home. Hirelings eat no food; the fee is everything. An escorted cargo drops its theft risk to 0, same as a soldier escort.

conflict.notes: Attacker and defender each roll one die per unit, modified by weapons and armour. Both sides apply hits simultaneously.

conditions.name: Prosperity
conditions.summary: Points for fed population, completed buildings and luxury goods held at game end.

conditions.name: Industry
conditions.summary: Points for the depth of your longest completed production chain and for each tier-3 good produced.

conditions.name: Network
conditions.summary: Points for towns connected by road, rail and sea routes you built.

victory.notes: Scoring is deliberately plural so that a mining-and-rail strategy and a farming-and-trade strategy can both win.
